reference: Takahashi H et al. Simultaneous Control of Venous Reservoir Level and Arterial Flow Rate in Cardiopulmonary Bypass With a Centrifugal Pump. IEEE J Transl Eng Health Med. 2023;11:435–440.
verified_from_sources: Final article: measured venous flow, arterial flow and reservoir level; arterial occluder actuation
Final article: nested feedforward/PID flow controller and I-PD reservoir controller
Final Eq.1: nonlinear occluder map; Eq.2: first-order lag with dead time
Author preprint Eq.5: third-order reference model; sigma=3.6 s in experimental setup
Final article: reservoir target 0.45 L; original sampling interval 0.01 s

implemented_components.mapping: Final Eq.1, beta=A*(R+delta_R0); caller must supply independently calibrated parameters
implemented_components.validation: Independent direct-form equivalence and inverse round-trip tests

implemented_components.mapping: Author preprint Eq.5, exact zero-order-hold update of three cascaded lags
implemented_components.validation: Analytic third-order step response and timestep refinement tests

adaptation_changes: Current comparison uses common pump-flow actuation, not the source occluder/feedforward/PID inner loop
I-PD gains are chosen on development cases; they are not claimed to be the authors' gains
Conventional positive derivative damping is an explicit design choice; the extracted preprint PD sign must be checked against the supplement
Derivative filtering, anti-windup, startup states and shared flow/slew limits are engineering choices
1-second sampling, adult-like synthetic plant and reference-assisted level correction differ from the source experiment
An explicit noisy venous-flow sensor is added to both comparison arms; legacy Sentinel is kept as a separate information ablation
Source controller tracks venous flow/level; Sentinel targets oxygen delivery/floor. Different objectives are kept visible; no global winner is certified

Implement and verify the full source feedforward/PID inner loop and experimental protocol
